## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Why

`scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py` builds MRoPE ids in `build_inputs` by calling `MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions` on a `types.SimpleNamespace(spatial_merge_size=merge_size)` and on `hf_in["input_ids"]`.

The method reads `self.patch_order` first and raises `ValueError` unless it is `"block"`. The stand-in has no `patch_order`, so the call raises `AttributeError` before that check. The real collator default is `"block"`.

The method docstring says `tokens` is `(num_tokens,)`. It does `tokens.unsqueeze(0)` and later returns `mrope_positions.squeeze(0)`, shape `(num_tokens, 3)`. `processor.apply_chat_template(..., return_tensors="pt")` yields `input_ids` of shape `(1, S)`. Unsqueeze makes that `(1, 1, S)`, and `batch_size, seq_len = tokens.shape` raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)`.

`Qwen35Model.forward` does not index `positions` itself. It passes them to each layer. `MRoPE._reshape_cache` uses the 3-axis cache only when `positions.ndim == 2` and the last dimension is 3, i.e. `(num_tokens, 3)`. The collator already returns that rank after `squeeze(0)`, and `preprocess_inputs` forwards the same rank. A stored `(1, S, 3)` tensor would skip MRoPE and fall through to plain RoPE. The old script comment asked for `(1, S, 3)`; that comment does not match the index. The forward comment that still says `(batch, seq, 3)` is the same mismatch and is left alone.

`vision_to_patches` returns `grid_thw` of shape `(3,)`. The collator indexes `grid_thw[image_index]` as one image's `(t, h, w)`, so `grid_thw.unsqueeze(0)` to `(num_images, 3)` stays.

**Example.**

```python
mrope_builder = types.SimpleNamespace(spatial_merge_size=2)
MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions(
    mrope_builder,
    torch.zeros(1, 5, dtype=torch.long),  # HF input_ids
    torch.zeros(1, 3),
    None,
    None,
    image_token_id=99,
    video_token_id=98,
)
# AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'patch_order'
```

With `patch_order="block"` but the same `(1, 5)` tokens:

```text
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

`build_inputs` now squeezes the processor row to `(S,)` before the collator call, so positions come back `(S, 3)`. `tt_inputs` stores that row and `patches` of shape `(N, P)`. `run_tt` reads packed `(T, V)` logits.

## What changed

- `build_inputs` sets `patch_order="block"`, squeezes `hf_in["input_ids"]` to `(S,)`, and calls `MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions` inline. The one-off helper is gone.
- Stored tensors match the packed forward: tokens `(S,)`, patches `(N, P)`, `grid_thw` `(num_images, 3)`, positions `(S, 3)`. `patches.unsqueeze(0)` is gone. `grid_thw.unsqueeze(0)` stays.
- `run_tt`'s reference SDPA takes packed `(T, H, K)` the way `FlexInnerAttention` does: `transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0)` to `(1, H, T, K)`, then the inverse. `transpose(1, 2)` was the old `(B, L, H, K)` layout.
- Last-token logits are `logits[-1:].unsqueeze(0)`, shape `(1, 1, V)`, matching `run_hf`.
- Deleted `tests/unit_tests/cpu/scripts/test_qwen35_numerical_mrope.py`. It grepped the script and skipped on import.

`mm_collator.py` is unchanged. The `model.half()` / `to_empty` / `init_states` order in `run_tt` is unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep a helper that accepts both `(S,)` and `(1, S)`. No. `build_inputs` is the only caller and it owns the processor row.
- Leave `run_tt` on batched `(1, S)` tokens and `(1, N, P)` patches. No. The vision encoder checks `pixel_values.shape[0]` against the patch grid, and the text forward is packed `(num_tokens,)`.
- Leave `_SDPA` on `transpose(1, 2)`. No. That swaps heads with `head_dim` once Q/K/V are `(T, H, K)`. GQA then sees different query and key embedding sizes.
- Make `_build_mrope_positions` treat a missing `patch_order` as `"block"`. No. The method already requires `"block"`. #5728 owns `mm_collator.py`.
- Unsqueeze positions to `(1, S, 3)`. No. Rank 3 is not the MRoPE path in `MRoPE._reshape_cache`.
- Construct a real `MultiModalCollator`. No. That needs a dataset context and a tokenizer.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `build_inputs` raises `AttributeError` because the MRoPE stand-in has no `patch_order` | The stand-in sets `patch_order="block"` |
| Processor `input_ids` `(1, S)` make `_build_mrope_positions` raise `ValueError` on the shape unpack | The call gets a 1-D row. Stored positions are `(S, 3)` |
| `run_tt` passes tokens `(1, S)` and patches `(1, N, P)` into a packed forward | tokens `(S,)`, patches `(N, P)` |
| `logits[:, -1:, :]` assumes 3-D logits | `logits[-1:].unsqueeze(0)` matches HF `(1, 1, V)` |
| No config or CLI flag | No config or CLI flag |

## Numerics

Not run. The script needs a downloaded Qwen3.5 checkpoint and a GPU. This does not change a training step. It changes the script's forward shapes so that check can run.

## Testing

`py_compile` of `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py` succeeded with `/opt/homebrew/anaconda3/bin/python`. The script was not executed. There is no local checkpoint and no GPU.

The CPU test file was removed. It AST-walked the source, asserted `AttributeError` for a missing attribute, and turned import errors into skips. An existing `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/qwen3_5/test_qwen3_5_mrope_positions.py` already locks the `(num_tokens, 3)` contract. This machine still cannot collect that file (`spmd_types` has no `rules`).

## Known issues / follow-ups

#5153 is open and edits this script only around model construction: it moves `model.half()` before `to_empty` / `init_states` and factors `_build_tt_model`. This PR does not touch those lines. The SDPA and logit-index edits are later in `run_tt`.

#5728 edits `mm_collator.py`. This PR does not.

`Qwen35Model.forward` still comments that multimodal `positions` are `(batch, seq, 3)`. `MRoPE._reshape_cache` and `preprocess_inputs` use `(num_tokens, 3)`. Not changed here. Open PRs already edit `model.py`.

**What this PR does.** In `numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py`, it adds `patch_order="block"` to the `SimpleNamespace` stand-in for the collator. It also adds a helper that squeezes the HF `input_ids` from `(1, S)` to `(S,)` before calling `MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions`, so positions come back as `(S, 3)`, the rank that `MRoPE._reshape_cache` dispatches on. **Example.**
```python

_build_mrope_positions(SimpleNamespace(spatial_merge_size=2), ids_1S, ...)  # AttributeError
# this PR: build_inputs passes; then run_tt
model(ids_1S, pixel_values=patches_1NP, positions=pos_S3, ...)
#   _prepare_multimodal_embeds -> (1, S, D); Qwen35Attention: num_tokens = x_TD.shape[0] == 1

1. The `## Summary (human-written)` section is empty. The author needs to write it.

3. `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py:84-123` -- the single-use helper isn't needed once `input_ids` is squeezed at the source. Inline the call again.

Not verified: the `run_tt` failure was found by reading the code (`model.py:158`, `:598`, `multimodal.py:144`), not by running it on a GPU.

The positions are fixed, but the `tt_inputs` tuple built a few lines below still stores `hf_in["input_ids"]` as `(1, S)` and `patches.unsqueeze(0)` as `(1, N, P)`. `run_tt` passes both to `Qwen35Model.forward`, and that forward is packed now: `_prepare_multimodal_embeds` returns `(num_tokens, dim)`, `Qwen35Attention.forward` reads `num_tokens = x_TD.shape[0]`, and `get_vision_positions` / `scatter_vision_embeds` expect `(T,)` / `(T, D)`. The fix: squeeze once at the source and store packed tensors. For example `input_ids_S = hf_in["input_ids"].squeeze(0)`, then use it in both this call and `tt_inputs`, store `patches` without the `unsqueeze(0)`, and use `logits[-1:]` in `run_tt`. ## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Why

`scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py` builds MRoPE ids in `build_inputs` by calling `MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions` on a `types.SimpleNamespace(spatial_merge_size=merge_size)` and on `hf_in["input_ids"]`.

The method reads `self.patch_order` first and raises `ValueError` unless it is `"block"`. The stand-in has no `patch_order`, so the call raises `AttributeError` before that check. The real collator default is `"block"`.

The method docstring says `tokens` is `(num_tokens,)`. It does `tokens.unsqueeze(0)` and later returns `mrope_positions.squeeze(0)`, shape `(num_tokens, 3)`. `processor.apply_chat_template(..., return_tensors="pt")` yields `input_ids` of shape `(1, S)`. Unsqueeze makes that `(1, 1, S)`, and `batch_size, seq_len = tokens.shape` raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)`.

`Qwen35Model.forward` does not index `positions` itself. It passes them to each layer. `MRoPE._reshape_cache` uses the 3-axis cache only when `positions.ndim == 2` and the last dimension is 3, i.e. `(num_tokens, 3)`. The collator already returns that rank after `squeeze(0)`, and `preprocess_inputs` forwards the same rank. A stored `(1, S, 3)` tensor would skip MRoPE and fall through to plain RoPE. The old script comment asked for `(1, S, 3)`; that comment does not match the index. The forward comment that still says `(batch, seq, 3)` is the same mismatch and is left alone.

`vision_to_patches` returns `grid_thw` of shape `(3,)`. The collator indexes `grid_thw[image_index]` as one image's `(t, h, w)`, so `grid_thw.unsqueeze(0)` to `(num_images, 3)` stays.

**Example.**

```python
mrope_builder = types.SimpleNamespace(spatial_merge_size=2)
MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions(
    mrope_builder,
    torch.zeros(1, 5, dtype=torch.long),  # HF input_ids
    torch.zeros(1, 3),
    None,
    None,
    image_token_id=99,
    video_token_id=98,
)
# AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'patch_order'
```

With `patch_order="block"` but the same `(1, 5)` tokens:

```text
ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)
```

`build_inputs` now squeezes the processor row to `(S,)` before the collator call, so positions come back `(S, 3)`. `tt_inputs` stores that row and `patches` of shape `(N, P)`. `run_tt` reads packed `(T, V)` logits.

## What changed

- `build_inputs` sets `patch_order="block"`, squeezes `hf_in["input_ids"]` to `(S,)`, and calls `MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions` inline. The one-off helper is gone.
- Stored tensors match the packed forward: tokens `(S,)`, patches `(N, P)`, `grid_thw` `(num_images, 3)`, positions `(S, 3)`. `patches.unsqueeze(0)` is gone. `grid_thw.unsqueeze(0)` stays.
- `run_tt`'s reference SDPA takes packed `(T, H, K)` the way `FlexInnerAttention` does: `transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0)` to `(1, H, T, K)`, then the inverse. `transpose(1, 2)` was the old `(B, L, H, K)` layout.
- Last-token logits are `logits[-1:].unsqueeze(0)`, shape `(1, 1, V)`, matching `run_hf`.
- Deleted `tests/unit_tests/cpu/scripts/test_qwen35_numerical_mrope.py`. It grepped the script and skipped on import.

`mm_collator.py` is unchanged. The `model.half()` / `to_empty` / `init_states` order in `run_tt` is unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep a helper that accepts both `(S,)` and `(1, S)`. No. `build_inputs` is the only caller and it owns the processor row.
- Leave `run_tt` on batched `(1, S)` tokens and `(1, N, P)` patches. No. The vision encoder checks `pixel_values.shape[0]` against the patch grid, and the text forward is packed `(num_tokens,)`.
- Leave `_SDPA` on `transpose(1, 2)`. No. That swaps heads with `head_dim` once Q/K/V are `(T, H, K)`. GQA then sees different query and key embedding sizes.
- Make `_build_mrope_positions` treat a missing `patch_order` as `"block"`. No. The method already requires `"block"`. #5728 owns `mm_collator.py`.
- Unsqueeze positions to `(1, S, 3)`. No. Rank 3 is not the MRoPE path in `MRoPE._reshape_cache`.
- Construct a real `MultiModalCollator`. No. That needs a dataset context and a tokenizer.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `build_inputs` raises `AttributeError` because the MRoPE stand-in has no `patch_order` | The stand-in sets `patch_order="block"` |
| Processor `input_ids` `(1, S)` make `_build_mrope_positions` raise `ValueError` on the shape unpack | The call gets a 1-D row. Stored positions are `(S, 3)` |
| `run_tt` passes tokens `(1, S)` and patches `(1, N, P)` into a packed forward | tokens `(S,)`, patches `(N, P)` |
| `logits[:, -1:, :]` assumes 3-D logits | `logits[-1:].unsqueeze(0)` matches HF `(1, 1, V)` |
| No config or CLI flag | No config or CLI flag |

## Numerics

Not run. The script needs a downloaded Qwen3.5 checkpoint and a GPU. This does not change a training step. It changes the script's forward shapes so that check can run.

## Testing

`py_compile` of `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py` succeeded with `/opt/homebrew/anaconda3/bin/python`. The script was not executed. There is no local checkpoint and no GPU.

The CPU test file was removed. It AST-walked the source, asserted `AttributeError` for a missing attribute, and turned import errors into skips. An existing `tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/qwen3_5/test_qwen3_5_mrope_positions.py` already locks the `(num_tokens, 3)` contract. This machine still cannot collect that file (`spmd_types` has no `rules`).

## Known issues / follow-ups

#5153 is open and edits this script only around model construction: it moves `model.half()` before `to_empty` / `init_states` and factors `_build_tt_model`. This PR does not touch those lines. The SDPA and logit-index edits are later in `run_tt`.

#5728 edits `mm_collator.py`. This PR does not.

`Qwen35Model.forward` still comments that multimodal `positions` are `(batch, seq, 3)`. `MRoPE._reshape_cache` and `preprocess_inputs` use `(num_tokens, 3)`. Not changed here. Open PRs already edit `model.py`.

**Verdict: Request changes** -- this fixes the MRoPE positions, but the script still can't run: `run_tt` passes batched `(1, S)` inputs to a model that now takes packed `(T,)` tokens.

**What this PR does.** In `numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py`, it adds `patch_order="block"` to the `SimpleNamespace` stand-in for the collator. It also adds a helper that squeezes the HF `input_ids` from `(1, S)` to `(S,)` before calling `MultiModalCollator._build_mrope_positions`, so positions come back as `(S, 3)`, the rank that `MRoPE._reshape_cache` dispatches on. It also adds a 150-line CPU test file. The diagnosis of the two errors is correct (`mm_collator.py:218`, `:230-232`).

**Example.**
```python
# main: build_inputs
_build_mrope_positions(SimpleNamespace(spatial_merge_size=2), ids_1S, ...)  # AttributeError
# this PR: build_inputs passes; then run_tt
model(ids_1S, pixel_values=patches_1NP, positions=pos_S3, ...)
#   _prepare_multimodal_embeds -> (1, S, D); Qwen35Attention: num_tokens = x_TD.shape[0] == 1
logits[:, -1:, :]   # model returns (T, V): too many indices
```

### Must fix
1. The `## Summary (human-written)` section is empty. The author needs to write it.
2. `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py:205` -- the tensors stored in `tt_inputs` and read in `run_tt` (tokens `(1, S)`, `patches.unsqueeze(0)`, `logits[:, -1:, :]`) still use the old batched layout. The real problem is that this script was never migrated to packed 1-D tokens. Fixing positions alone moves the failure from `build_inputs` to `run_tt`. Migrate the whole script, and run it once against a checkpoint. "Numerics: Not run" isn't enough for a script whose only job is a numerics check.
3. `scripts/checkpoint_conversion/numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py:84-123` -- the single-use helper isn't needed once `input_ids` is squeezed at the source. Inline the call again.
4. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/scripts/test_qwen35_numerical_mrope.py` -- delete it. It greps source code, retests Python attribute lookup, and turns import failures into skips.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

The smallest correct change is roughly 10 lines, all in `numerical_tests_qwen3_5.py`:
- `build_inputs`: add `patch_order="block"`; `input_ids_S = hf_in["input_ids"].squeeze(0)`; pass `input_ids_S` to the existing inline `_build_mrope_positions` call; store `(input_ids_S, patches, grid_thw.unsqueeze(0), mrope_positions)`.

The custom `_SDPA` in `run_tt` already works with `THK` (`transpose(1, 2)` gives `(H, T, K)`), so it should not need changes. *Unverified*: whether anything else in the forward still assumes a batch dim. Running the script will show that.

The stale `(batch, seq, 3)` comment at `torchtitan/models/qwen3_5/model.py:714-715` comes from the same packed-layout migration. A one-line fix to `(num_tokens, 3)` / `(num_tokens,)` could go in this PR, since it is the same contract.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** The script now passes packed tensors end to end (`build_inputs` -> `run_tt` -> `compare`), and every code item from the last review is resolved.

**What changed since the last review (617a6af).** `build_inputs` squeezes `input_ids` once to `(S,)` and calls `_build_mrope_positions` inline, so positions come back as `(S, 3)`. `tt_inputs` stores `(S,)` tokens, `(N, P)` patches, and a `(1, 3)` grid. `run_tt` takes `logits[-1:].unsqueeze(0)`, which matches HF's `(1, 1, V)`.
